newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKS COME BACK TO KNOT SERIES ON BASES-FULL WALK.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKS COME BACK TO KNOT SERIES ON BASES-FULL WALK.

text.p: Steve Avery walked in the go-ahead run as the New York Yankees came back from a 6-0 deficit to beat the Atlanta Braves 8-6 in 10 innings and even the World Series at two games apiece on Wednesday.

The Yankees, who had tied the game on Jim Leyritz's three-run homer in the eighth inning, used the "little ball" manager Joe Torre says they must rely on against the defending champions to earn a victory that ensures the best-of-seven series will return to New York after Thursday's Game 5 here.

In the 10th, with two outs, Tim Raines walked and Derek Jeter singled. Atlanta manager Bobby Cox then told Avery to intentionally walk Bernie Williams to load the bases -- putting the go-ahead run just 90 feet away from the plate.
Cox called it the "smart thing to do," asking: "Why not? He's the best hitter they've got."

Torre sent up pinch-hitter Wade Boggs for Andy Fox, who had been inserted in the ninth as a pinch-runner. The veteran known for his accurate eye, drew the walk -- after a checked-swing ball 2 on a 1-2 count that drew howls from the crowd.
"We blew the game, Ave didn't blow anything," Cox said, defending Avery.
New York added another run on an error when Ryan Klesko -- just inserted in a double switch to bring in Brad Clontz to pitch -- could not handle Charlie Hayes's low bloop to first base.
"A lot of things went wrong for us tonight," said Cox. "We'll bounce back."

Australian Graeme Lloyd got the win, facing two batters and throwing nine pitches to get a double play in the bottom of the ninth and a strikeout to begin the 10th. John Wetteland picked up his second save in as many nights for getting the last two outs of the game.
